But the text says Nadab and Abihu died before their father did, “…and they had no sons; so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.” That's the heavy part of this list, and I think it's worth a quiet moment. So the priests come down through Eleazar and Ithamar, not through those two.

explanations.answer: By letting the oldest go first
explanations.explanation: Oldest first sounds sensible, friend. Here's the thing, though. The text says they were divided by lot, and at the end it says the family heads and their younger brothers cast lots alike (1 Chronicles 24:31). So being older didn't move anybody up the line.

explanations.answer: Both sides had officers of the sanctuary
explanations.explanation: That's the reason the text gives. It says “there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God among both Eleazar's and Ithamar's descendants.” So both sides had what the work needed, and both went into the same drawing. Having more people doesn't earn you more turns.

explanations.answer: Ithamar's side asked to be included
explanations.explanation: That makes a good story, friend, a smaller side speaking up. But the text never says anyone asked. It gives the reason instead: there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God among both Eleazar's and Ithamar's descendants. That's why both sides were in.

explanations.answer: The king wanted to honor Ithamar
explanations.explanation: I can see why you'd think so, baker, since David was the one running things. But the text doesn't say David wanted to honor anybody here. It says both sides had officers of the sanctuary and officers of God. That's the reason both were in.

explanations.answer: They cast lots like the priests
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The text says “As their brothers the descendants of Aaron did, they also cast lots in the presence of King David and of Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the families of the priests and Levites.” Same method for everybody. The king and those leaders were right there for it.

explanations.answer: They let the king choose for them
explanations.explanation: David was standing right there, so I see why you'd pick him, friend. But the text doesn't say he chose anything. It says the Levite families “also cast lots” just as the priests did. David was there as they cast them.

explanations.answer: They let the scribe pick for them
explanations.explanation: The scribe Shemaiah was busy writing, so he's an easy name to land on. But the text says the Levite families “also cast lots” as their brothers the priests did. Nobody is said to pick for them. The scribe's job was writing names down (1 Chronicles 24:6).
